parallel.requirements: The parallel run recognized the ESM .mjs output requirement, local-import restriction, manual argv parsing, canonical JSON behavior, Python bytes repr, and use of /workspace/dataset/test7_executable for probing.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent spawned cli_probe and encoding_probe, continued probing locally, wrote its own implementation, and later reconciled child side effects; ownership of /output/test7.mjs was not isolated across live actors.
parallel.implementation: The parent delivered modules for CLI parsing, help text, program name, canonical value serialization, string escaping, code-point ordering, byte encoding, Python bytes repr, and test7.mjs.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integration ended with the parent deleting duplicate child-created files and restoring the parent-selected test7.mjs and library tree before returning a full final code listing.
parallel.verification: Parallel ran many executable and Node spot checks, a final normalized parity sweep, node --check, Unicode sorting checks, and quote-heavy bytes repr checks before closure.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed 47 of 153 cases. The directly visible ordinary risk is that parity checks normalized the program name in argparse help/error text, while exact hidden evaluator requirements may have treated those lines differently.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same ESM .mjs, local import, manual argv parsing, canonical JSON, Python bytes repr, and executable-probing requirements from the shared prompt.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One agent owned probing, implementation, verification, and final reporting. There were no child agents or shared workspace ownership conflicts.
serial.implementation: The serial run created argvUtils, cli, unicodeOrder, canonicalJson, pythonBytesRepr, index, and test7.mjs modules and wired the entry point through the library exports.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial implementation was written as one coordinated tree and final output listed the library files and entry file without later cleanup or overwrite reconciliation.
serial.verification: Serial ran executable probes, Node spot checks, and a broader automated parity sweep that normalized the program name in help/error output before finalizing.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation failed 47 of 153 cases. The final response itself acknowledged a program-name difference in usage/error text, and no parallel coordination issue was present in this control.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized pure ESM, .mjs placement, manual --a/--b parsing, local-only imports, canonical JSON bytes, Python bytes repr, and executable probing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same requirements and tested the same broad behavior classes, including argparse edge cases and non-ASCII canonical output.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement recognition was materially similar; both missed or accepted the same likely exact-output risk around usage/error program naming, producing the same official score.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split exploration into children while the parent also implemented; at least one child expanded into a full independent implementation in the shared output directory.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept probing, implementation, verification, and delivery under a single owner and wrote one coherent module tree.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel split created overlapping implementation ownership of the required deliverable, while serial had no ownership collision.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child task content is encrypted in the ledger, but observable behavior shows the children did not have isolated output ownership and wrote competing module layouts.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial did not need handoff or cross-agent interfaces because the same actor carried executable observations into one implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The concrete difference is not a proven missing brief; it is that parallel lacked an effective shared-output boundary and serial avoided that interface entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent implemented a detailed module split for parser, canonical serializer, code-point sorting, bytes repr, and entry file, then restored that implementation after child side effects.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented a similar functional set through a flatter module split and kept that single code path through verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implementation paths aimed at the same semantics and both failed official evaluation equally; the notable parallel-specific difference was duplicate implementation churn, not a different core algorithm.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel waited for children, polled agent state, saw result snippets, then interrupted remaining children during cleanup after the parent had enough behavioral data.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle and instead polled only its own long-running parity sweep session.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had active child lifecycle management and cleanup, including interrupted children; serial avoided all child join and takeover decisions.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had a real shared-state conflict: parent and child implementations wrote `/output/test7.mjs` and alternate libraries, and the parent later cleaned the final tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote and verified one output tree, with final files listed and no competing writer or cleanup event.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel run had an adverse deliverable overwrite and reconciliation episode; the serial control had none.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran sample checks, parser edge checks, normalized parity checks, node --check, Unicode sorting, and bytes repr checks, then returned a final response.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran similar executable probes and an automated parity sweep that normalized the program name in help/error text before final delivery.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Verification depth was similar and both official evaluations failed equally; both accepted normalized program-name differences rather than proving strict end-to-end official parity.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used four subagents, 113 LLM requests, and 250 tool calls over about 510 agent seconds, but did not hit the host timeout and closed after cleanup.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents, 30 LLM requests, and 82 tool calls over about 278 agent seconds, closing after a single parity sweep and file review.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent substantially more coordination and tool budget because of child work and overwrite cleanup, while serial was shorter; the official outcome nevertheless stayed the same.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome: the current completed status evaluations show both parallel and serial failed with 106 of 153 tests passed. Both attempts implemented a manual ESM parser, canonical JSON encoder, Python bytes repr, and code-point sorting, and both verified many samples while normalizing or accepting the executable-versus-test7.mjs program-name difference in help and error output. The parallel run had an additional coordination defect, a child overwrite of the deliverable, but the parent observed and repaired that state before delivery, so it is best treated as an adverse process episode rather than an evidenced cause of a different official result.
parallel_contributors: Parallel added coordination overhead and a shared-output overwrite that forced cleanup.
Parallel final verification normalized program-name differences instead of proving exact official CLI text parity.
serial_contributors: Serial avoided child write collisions by keeping one implementation owner.
Serial also accepted an expected program-name difference, so it did not outperform parallel on the official evaluation.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The two runs used different module layouts, but both encoded the same intended behaviors and both scored 106/153.
Both likely retained an exact-output gap around argparse program names, but the pair evidence does not isolate hidden testcase failures to that single cause.
evaluator_effects: Parallel cell/evaluation/summary.json is stale from an incomplete first evaluator invocation; the completed retry under cell/status.json is the outcome source.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is parallel adverse but not outcome differential
